documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT
42F graphic designer transferring care; liked the idea of being able to text her doctor. Prior office records reviewed (filed 7/8).

Hypothyroidism: on levothyroxine 75 mcg for years, takes it first thing with water, coffee 30-40 min later. Energy fine, no cold intolerance, no constipation, periods regular. Last TSH 2023 in range per old records.

Weight: has carried extra weight since her late 20s. Mostly desk-bound for work; walks on weekends, tried a few apps. Wants to work on it but not interested in medication right now.

PMH: hypothyroidism, obesity.
PSH: tonsillectomy age 7; cholecystectomy ~2017.
Meds: levothyroxine 75 mcg qAM.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother hypothyroid; father type 2 DM.
SH: never smoker, a glass of wine or two a week, no drugs. Works from a home studio and some days in an office in town.

ROS: negative for chest pain, palpitations, dyspnea, GI or GU complaints, rash, numbness, mood change.

EXAM
Vitals as recorded; BMI about 34.
Well-appearing, pleasant. Thyroid not enlarged, no nodules felt. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, well-healed small surgical scars. No edema. Affect bright. PHQ-2 0.

ASSESSMENT / PLAN
1. Hypothyroidism - clinically euthyroid. Continue levothyroxine 75 mcg. TSH today.
2. Obesity, BMI ~34 - talked through small steps: a lunchtime walk, fewer evening snacks, aiming for 5% over a year. A1c and lipids today given her dad's diabetes.
3. Health maintenance - HIV and hep C screens once, today. Mammogram ordered (none since turning 40). Pap/HPV 2022 normal, next 2027. Tdap 2019. Flu and COVID this fall.

RTC for a physical next summer, sooner as needed.

No changes. The mammogram order is in; scheduling should reach out, or you can call them directly.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: About 7 wks of pins-and-needles in the R hand, mostly thumb through ring finger. Worst at night, shakes the hand out to get back to sleep. Notices it after long sessions on the tablet and mouse. No neck pain, no fall or injury, L hand fine. Thyroid meds unchanged.

O: Vitals as charted. Neck nontender, full ROM, no pain with rotation. R hand: reports reduced feel at the thumb and index fingertips to light touch. Skin normal, no swelling.

A/P: R hand paresthesias, median-nerve pattern most likely. Neurology referral placed for evaluation. In the meantime, keep the wrist straight while working, take breaks.
Flu and updated COVID vaccine given today, tolerated.
TSH was normal in July.

documents.title: Neurology Consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT NEUROLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 11/21/2024
Reason for referral: right hand sensory symptoms (referred by her primary care physician)

HISTORY
Ms. Hanlon is a 42-year-old right-handed graphic designer who has had steadily increasing numbness and tingling in the right hand over roughly three months. She describes intermittent burning and pins and needles in the thumb, index and middle fingers and the thumb side of the ring finger. Symptoms are worse overnight and occasionally wake her. Over the past few weeks she has been dropping things more often, which she has noticed at her drawing desk. The symptoms are getting in the way of her work at the keyboard and tablet. She has had no neck pain, injury, or weakness in the left arm.

Past history: hypothyroidism, obesity. Surgeries: tonsillectomy in childhood, cholecystectomy.
Medications: levothyroxine 75 mcg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: hypothyroidism in her mother; type 2 diabetes in her father.
Social: never smoker; drinks socially, one or two a week.

EXAMINATION
Alert, fluent, cranial nerves normal. Right hand: diminished light touch and pinprick over the palmar thumb and index finger. Mild flattening of the thenar eminence. Weakness of right thumb abduction and opposition. Tinel sign at the wrist and Phalen maneuver did not reproduce symptoms. Strength, tone, reflexes and sensation otherwise normal in all four limbs; gait and coordination normal.

IMPRESSION
Right carpal tunnel syndrome, with sensory loss in the median distribution and early thenar involvement.

RECOMMENDATIONS
- Neutral-position wrist splint at night.
- Workstation changes: keyboard and mouse at elbow height, wrist kept straight, short breaks every hour.
- Return or contact us if symptoms progress.

Thank you for this referral.
Outpatient neurology

documents.title: Wrist brace
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi - the neurologist said to wear a wrist splint at night. Does it matter which one? The drugstore has like six kinds. Also wondering if I need a prescription for insurance.

documents.title: RE: Wrist brace
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good question. Look for one with a stiff bar on the palm side that holds the wrist flat, not bent back. An over-the-counter one is fine and usually cheaper than going through insurance. Wear it every night for at least a few weeks before judging it. Let me know how it goes.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL, 43F

Interval: Saw neurology in November for the R hand, told carpal tunnel. Has worn an OTC night splint most nights since December. Says the night waking is less frequent but the tingling is still there most days, more after deadline weeks. Raised the monitor, bought a vertical mouse. Doesn't want anything more done right now.
Thyroid: no symptoms, taking levothyroxine faithfully.
Weight up a couple of pounds over the year; busy stretch at work, less walking.

Meds: levothyroxine 75 mcg daily. NKDA.
SH unchanged: never smoker, 1-2 drinks/wk.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: vitals in flowsheet. NAD. Thyroid normal size. RRR, lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender. R hand: grossly normal appearance; she reports less feeling in the thumb and index pads. No edema. Mood good, PHQ-2 0.

A/P
- Hypothyroidism: stable. TSH with today's draw; continue 75 mcg.
- Obesity, BMI ~34: revisited goals; she is going to try a weekday walking group near her office. Not interested in medication. A1c and lipids today.
- R carpal tunnel syndrome: partial response to splinting. Continue splint and ergonomic changes; she will message if grip or numbness worsens and we can send her to hand surgery.
- HM: mammogram ordered. Cervical screening next 2027. Flu and COVID in the fall. Colon screening starts at 45.

See in 6 months to check on the hand and thyroid.

reports.conclusion: BI-RADS 1: negative. Return to annual screening.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Subjective
R hand worse since about November despite wearing the splint nightly. Numb through much of the workday now, not just at night. Grip weaker - fumbling her stylus and pens. No neck pain, nothing in the L hand. Thyroid: feels well, no missed doses.

Objective
Vitals per flowsheet; weight down a little from summer.
Neck nontender. R hand: she reports reduced sensation in the thumb and index fingers; grip subjectively weaker on the right.

Assessment and plan
1. R carpal tunnel syndrome, progressing after more than a year of splinting. Referred to orthopedic hand surgery. Keep the splint on at night until then.
2. Hypothyroidism: TSH today, levothyroxine 75 mcg unchanged.
3. Obesity: walking group most weeks; encouraged.

Physical due in the summer.

documents.title: Orthopedic Hand Surgery Consultation
documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body:
ORTHOPEDIC HAND CLINIC - NEW PATIENT
Visit date: 05/06/2026
Referring: primary care

HPI: 44-year-old right-hand-dominant woman with hypothyroidism and obesity seen for the right hand. She was evaluated by neurology in 2024 for the same symptoms and has used a night splint since. Numbness and tingling are worse than before, still worst at night and sometimes waking her. New over the last months: trouble opening jars and keeping hold of a coffee mug because her grip has weakened. Works long hours at a keyboard.

Meds: levothyroxine 75 mcg daily. Allergies: NKDA.
PSH: tonsillectomy, cholecystectomy.
FH: mother hypothyroidism; father type 2 diabetes.

Exam, right hand and wrist: sensation decreased over the palmar thumb, index and middle fingers. Visible thenar muscle atrophy. Tapping over the volar wrist reproduces her paresthesias (Tinel positive). Phalen test positive at 30 seconds. Skin intact, full wrist and finger range of motion.

Assessment: right carpal tunnel syndrome with thenar atrophy.

Plan: nerve conduction study with EMG of both upper limbs to stage it. Given the atrophy we discussed surgical release, which she would like to pursue after the study. Risks and recovery reviewed.

Orthopedic Surgery, hand service

reports.text: Indication: right hand numbness with thenar atrophy. Hand temperature maintained above 32 C. Nerve conduction: right median sensory response absent across the wrist. Right median motor: distal latency 6.8 ms, recorded at abductor pollicis brevis; amplitude 2.1 mV. Right ulnar motor and sensory studies normal. Left median and left ulnar motor and sensory studies normal. Needle EMG: right abductor pollicis brevis shows fibrillation potentials and reduced recruitment. Remaining right C6-T1 muscles sampled are normal.
reports.conclusion: Severe right median mononeuropathy at the wrist. No electrodiagnostic evidence of cervical radiculopathy.

procedures.procedure: Nerve conduction study with needle EMG

documents.title: Operative Report - Right Carpal Tunnel Release
documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT SURGERY CENTER - OPERATIVE REPORT
Date of surgery: 06/17/2026
Preoperative diagnosis: right carpal tunnel syndrome, severe by electrodiagnostic testing
Postoperative diagnosis: same
Procedure: right open carpal tunnel release
Anesthesia: local with monitored sedation, upper arm tourniquet
Allergies: NKDA

Findings: the transverse carpal ligament was divided completely. The median nerve beneath it was flattened, otherwise intact, with no mass in the canal.

Description: the right upper limb was prepped and draped. A longitudinal palmar incision was made in line with the radial border of the ring finger. Palmar fascia divided, transverse carpal ligament released under direct vision from proximal to distal, protecting the nerve and its motor branch. Hemostasis after tourniquet release. Skin closed with nylon sutures, soft bulky dressing applied.

Estimated blood loss minimal. No complications. Discharged home the same morning in stable condition.

Orthopedic Surgery, hand service

events.reason: Post-op check, right carpal tunnel release

documents.title: Orthopedic Post-operative Visit
documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body:
HAND CLINIC - POST-OP
Date: 07/01/2026, two weeks after right open carpal tunnel release.

She is pleased: the nighttime numbness and waking have stopped. Daytime tingling much reduced. Thumb still feels weak.

Exam: incision healed, sutures removed today. No signs of infection. Thenar atrophy and weakness of thumb abduction unchanged at this stage.

Plan: hand therapy referral for scar care and strengthening. Explained that thenar muscle recovery is slow and may be incomplete after severe compression. Return in 3 months.

Orthopedic Surgery, hand service

documents.title: Surgery update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just a heads-up that I had the carpal tunnel surgery in June. Sleeping through the night for the first time in ages! Starting hand therapy next week. Thumb is still weak but they said that takes a while.

documents.title: RE: Surgery update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great news, thanks for letting me know - I have the surgeon's notes. Stick with the therapy. We'll catch up at your physical in September.
